latest_rss.title: A Pair of Straw Sandals: Tracing the Long March memory in Yudu
latest_rss.summary: A few strands of straw are twisted, woven, and bound together. Little by little, they take the shape of a pair of sandals. Simple as they are, these straw sandals carry a history that stretches back more than 90 years.These sandals are closely associated with the Red Army soldiers who gathered there before embarking on the Long March. Yudu County in Southeastern China's Jiangxi Province was one of the important gathering and departure points of the Central Red Army. In 1934, tens of thousands of people from the county joined the Red Army. Almost every family in Yudu has one that joined the Red Army.For those who made and offered them, the sandals were more than just footwear. They were a simple but practical way of supporting soldiers embarking on a journey with an uncertain destination."These are the straw sandals the Red Army wore," said Xiao Nandou, an 82-year-old local straw-sandal weaver who still knows how to make them. It offers no comparable rule when lawful action appears to threaten the constitutional structure the military serves. The first response is neither refusal nor resignation, but rather deliberative friction.Deliberative friction is the professional duty to raise a credible constitutional concern in a form that remains attributable and survives the decision to execute.
